instruments.name: Keep it on your account
instruments.oneLiner: Money stays on your bank account: always there, never grows.
instruments.whatCanGoWrong: Nothing drops, but prices rise every year, so the same money buys less.

instruments.name: Savings deposit
instruments.oneLiner: The bank pays you a fixed rate for keeping your money for an agreed time.
instruments.whatCanGoWrong: The money is frozen for the term: break it early and you lose the interest.

instruments.name: Treasury bonds
instruments.oneLiner: You lend money to the state and get interest, a bit above inflation.
instruments.whatCanGoWrong: Prices move a little month to month, and selling before maturity can cost a fee.

instruments.name: S&P 500 ETF
instruments.oneLiner: One fund that holds the 500 biggest US companies at once.
instruments.whatCanGoWrong: The whole market can fall 10–20% in a bad year; it has always recovered, but not always fast.

instruments.name: NovaTech shares (one company)
instruments.oneLiner: A young company with one product, 3 years on the stock exchange.
instruments.whatCanGoWrong: One bad piece of news can cut the price in half overnight.
